correctness.rationale: The Calkin quotient forces the lower bound \(\delta=(M-m)/2\). For every \(arepsilon>0\), the spectral cutoff strictly below \(m-arepsilon\) is finite rank and the functional-calculus clipping produces a positive AN approximant within \(\delta+arepsilon\). At equality, the spectral projection below \(m\) gives an exact clipped positive AN minimizer precisely when finite rank; otherwise a vector orthogonal to the finite-dimensional lower spectral subspace of any candidate contradicts the norm bound. Boundary cases \(m=M\), \(m=0\), and nonseparable Hilbert spaces were checked. The imported positive AN spectral lemma was verified in primary full text, not assumed from a search snippet.

value.rationale: Best operator-norm approximation to the positive absolutely norm-attaining cone is natural because the cone is not closed and prior work characterizes only membership and closure. The result completely determines both the nonzero distance and whether an actual best approximant exists for every bounded positive Hilbert-space operator, including a sharp one-sided spectral threshold not determined by essential spectrum alone. Two operators with the same essential spectrum can have identical positive distances yet opposite nearest-point attainment, with explicit nontrivial positive-distance examples.
